title: Oil-Water Separator

introduction.definition: An oil–water separator removes free oil and settleable solids from wastewater by gravity. In a corrugated plate interceptor (CPI), packs of inclined plates give oil droplets only a short distance to rise; they coalesce on the plates and slide up to the oil layer, which is skimmed off, while solids slide down into the hopper.
applications: Workshops, car washes and fuel stations

pressure.title: Stokes' law sets the rise velocity
pressure.description: An oil droplet rises at v = g·d²·(ρw − ρo)/(18·μ) (Stokes). Small droplets rise very slowly, so the inclined plates give each droplet only a short distance to rise before it meets a plate surface, coalesces and slides up to the oil layer. CPI separators typically remove free oil droplets down to roughly 50–60 µm; API separators ~ 150 µm.

alignment: Weirs and launders set level so flow and overflow are even.

video_tutorials.title: Oil-Water Separator — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Oil-Water Separator.
An oil–water separator removes free oil and settleable solids from wastewater by gravity.

In a corrugated plate interceptor (CPI), packs of inclined plates give oil droplets only a short distance to rise; they coalesce on the plates and slide up to the oil layer, which is skimmed off, while solids slide down into the hopper.
Typical applications include refinery and terminal drainage; workshops, car washes and fuel stations; ballast and produced water pre-treatment.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Oil-Water Separator works.
Oily water enters through the inlet baffle.
It flows through the inclined plate pack.
Oil droplets rise and form a layer.
The skimmer removes the oil.
Clean water leaves under the oil baffle over the weir.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
An oil droplet rises at v = g·d²·(ρw − ρo)/(18·μ) (Stokes).

video_tutorials.title: Oil-Water Separator — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Oil-Water Separator.
Skim oil; check levels.
Desludge hopper; clean plates.
Inspect tank coating.
Watch for oil carry-over: sheen in effluent. Common cause: emulsified oil, overload, plates fouled.
Watch for sludge build-up: short-circuiting. Common cause: infrequent desludging.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
